description: The Hotmaps project, funded by Horizon 2020, built an open-source heating and cooling mapping and planning toolbox with a default open dataset for the EU28 at national and local level, developed with seven pilot areas including Aalborg, Frankfurt, Geneva and Milton Keynes; its final software release came in September 2020. The building stock repository gives national building characteristics by residential type (single-family houses, multi-family houses and apartment blocks) and service sector (offices, trade, education, health, hotels and restaurants, other), by construction period from before 1945 to after 2010, with data up to 2016 and nearly zero-energy building information. Hectare-level (100 m) rasters for EU28, Switzerland, Norway and Iceland give heated gross floor area, heated building volume and heat density for residential and non-residential buildings for 2015, derived statistically from census, population grid, European Settlement Map and OpenStreetMap data. Coverage: EU28 plus Switzerland, Norway and Iceland. Access: GitLab repositories. Licence: CC BY 4.0. Caveats: maps are statistical estimates that ignore local conditions, and the stock data end in 2016. Simulation uses are archetype and gridded floor area inputs for building stock, heat demand and district heating models. Related records: the EU Building Stock Observatory.
